title: Tenant-credited shadow siphon with drift gating
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a non-invasive shadowing pipeline ("siphon") that duplicates production requests to candidate models while enforcing per-tenant credit partitions and an automated drift-gating circuit. The goal is to enable sustained, affordable shadow traffic for long-running model evaluation and A/B style quality comparisons without exposing users to candidate outputs. The siphon must: 1) support request-weighted sampling and short-window burn-rate backpressure per tenant, 2) carry metadata to ensure KV cache affinity and avoid unnecessary cold-cache penalties, 3) integrate with console trace and cost dashboards, and 4) provide a metrics-driven auto-rollback/disable mechanism when candidate model metrics (latency, error-rate, prompt-sanity, or quality regressions computed via eval hooks) cross configurable thresholds.
implementation_plan: Add a lightweight siphon middleware in the gateway that duplicates requests to a separate shadow route asynchronously and tags them with tenant-credit tokens.
Implement tenant credit ledger and short-term token buckets in the mirroring service to enforce soft spend caps and sampling windows.
Introduce request-weighted sampling algorithm: sample probability = min(base_rate * request_cost_multiplier, tenant_budget_remaining_fraction).
Carry KV-cache-hint headers (prefix-hash, seq-len-estimate) to route shadow requests to warmed fast-paths where possible and avoid cold-cache amplification.
Expose telemetry counters: mirrored_tokens, mirrored_requests, dropped_due_to_credit, drift_alerts, sample_rate_per_tenant.
Add a drift-gating controller that subscribes to shadow evaluation metrics and transitions candidate model traffic to disabled when multiple concurrent signals fire.
Create admin APIs for operators to inject temporary credit allowances and to manually quarantine tenants for debugging.
Ship console views and per-tenant cost/time series; wire up alerts and automated tickets if mirrored spend exceeds thresholds.
Roll out canary in two phases: internal-only tenants -> low-volume external tenants -> wide internal shadowing. Monitor burn rate and false-positive drift signals.
Document public SDK/REST headers and operational runbook (confluence link included in comments).
acceptance_criteria: Siphon duplicates <= 1% of all production requests in initial rollout and honors tenant credit partitions.
Mirrored requests carry KV-cache-hint headers and measurable cache warm-up rate increases when enabled.
Dashboard shows per-tenant mirrored token usage and auto-gating events within 60s of rule triggers.
Drift-gating controller disables candidate model for a tenant when configured thresholds (latency P95 > baseline+200ms OR quality drop > 5%) persist for >2m.
Operators can temporarily increase a tenant's shadow allowance via admin API and see immediate effect in telemetry.
No user-facing latency regression or increased error-rate in production traffic during siphon operation.
Security review completed and audit logging enabled for mirrored payloads and admin actions.
test_plan: Unit tests for sampling math, credit ledger accounting, and KV-cache-hint propagation.
Integration test: simulated tenants with synthetic traffic and a fake candidate model to verify drop/backpressure and billing metrics.
Chaos test: introduce candidate model latency spikes and ensure drift-gating triggers and auto-disable within desired SLO window.
Load test: verify mirroring path can sustain additional peak QPS at configured sample rates without impacting gateway latency.
Security test: verify mirrored payloads are redacted per PII policy and that audit logs capture admin API calls.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Mirroring increases upstream cache churn causing production latency. Mitigation: carry cache-hint, throttle mirror rate when cache-affinity drops, and start on warmed pools only.

Risk: Tenants with misconfigured budgets exhaust credit and stop receiving shadowing, reducing eval coverage. Mitigation: provide alerting and temporary top-up admin action and conservative default budgets.
Risk: False-positive drift signals disable a healthy candidate. Mitigation: require multi-signal confirmation, short hysteresis windows, and operator override paths.
Risk: Cost blowouts from runaway sampling. Mitigation: global spend cap, per-tenant hard caps, and emergency circuit to pause all mirroring.
